'''Angelides''': {{legend0|#a5b0ff|40–50%}} {{legend0|#7996e2|50–60%}} {{legend0|#6674de|60–70%}} | title = [[Governor of California|Governor]] | before_election = [[Arnold Schwarzenegger]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Arnold Schwarzenegger]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) | turnout = 32.77% {{decrease}}28.43pp }} {{ElectionsCA}} The '''2006 California gubernatorial election''' occurred in the US state on November 7, 2006. The [[Partisan primary|primary election]]s took place on June 6, 2006. The incumbent [[California Republican Party|Republican]] [[Governor of California|Governor]], [[Arnold Schwarzenegger]], won re-election for his first and only full term. His main opponent was [[California State Treasurer]] [[Phil Angelides]], the [[California Democratic Party]] nominee. [[Peter Camejo]] was the California [[Green Party of California|Green Party]] nominee, [[Janice Jordan]] was the [[Peace and Freedom Party (United States)|Peace and Freedom Party]] nominee, [[Art Olivier]] was the California [[Libertarian Party of California|Libertarian Party]] nominee, and [[Edward C. Noonan]] was the California [[American Independent Party]] nominee. Under the [[California Constitution|state constitution]], the [[Governor of California|governor]] serves a four-year term, with a maximum [[Term limits in the United States|term limit]] of two four-year terms for life, regardless of whether or not they are consecutive or nonconsecutive. [[Arnold Schwarzenegger]] was elected in a [[2003 California recall|2003 recall election]] and served out the remainder of predecessor [[Gray Davis]]'s term ending in 2007; Schwarzenegger was therefore eligible to serve until 2011.{{cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/news/opinion/sunday/commentary/la-op-jeffe2jul02,0,1256025,print.story?coll=la-sunday-commentary|title=Think it can't get any wilder?|website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080619092345/http://www.latimes.com/news/opinion/sunday/commentary/la-op-jeffe2jul02%2C0%2C1256025%2Cprint.story?coll=la-sunday-commentary|archive-date=June 19, 2008|access-date=October 8, 2006}} As of {{CURRENTYEAR}}, this and the [[2006 California Insurance Commissioner election|concurrent Insurance Commissioner election]] mark the most recent time Republicans have won a statewide election in California, the most recent time a Republican was officially elected California governor, and the last election in which a California governor and lieutenant governor of opposite political parties were elected. Exit polls showed Schwarzenegger won the vote of [[White Americans|White]] (63%–32%) and [[Asian Americans]] (62%–37%), while Angelides won among [[African Americans]] (70%–27%) and [[Hispanic and Latino Americans|Latinos]] (56%–39%).{{Cite web|date=November 2006|title=Exit Polls|url=https://www.cnn.com/ELECTION/2006/pages/results/states/CA/G/00/epolls.0.html|url-status=live|website=cnn.com|publisher=CNN}} == Primary election == Bar graph of statewide results{{cite web |url=http://primary2006.ss.ca.gov/Returns/gov/00.htm |title=CA Secretary of State – Primary Election- Governor of California – Statewide |publisher=Primary2006.ss.ca.gov |access-date=2010-08-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080828124126/http://primary2006.ss.ca.gov/Returns/gov/00.htm |archive-date=2008-08-28 |url-status=dead }} Results by county{{cite web |url=http://primary2006.ss.ca.gov/Returns/gov/00.htm#cty |title=CA Secretary of State – Primary Election- Governor of California – Statewide |publisher=Primary2006.ss.ca.gov |access-date=2010-08-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080828124126/http://primary2006.ss.ca.gov/Returns/gov/00.htm#cty |archive-date=2008-08-28 |url-status=dead }} The period for candidate nominations closed on March 24, 2006. === Republican === ==== Candidates ==== * Jeffrey Burns – general contractor * Bill Chambers – railroad switchman * Robert C. Burns]] |votes = 57,652 |percentage = 3.01% }} {{Election box total no change| |votes = 1,916,099 |percentage = 100.00% }} {{Election box end}} === Democratic === ==== Candidates ==== * [[Phil Angelides]] – [[California State Treasurer]]; former State Democratic Chair and developer * [[Barbara Becnel]] – Executive Director of Neighborhood House of North Richmond; founder of Save [[Stanley Tookie Williams]] campaign * Joe Brouilette – high school teacher * Edie Bukewihge – writer and publisher * Jerald Gerst – physician * Vibert Greene – engineer * Frank Macaluso – medical doctor * Michael Strimling – attorney * [[Steve Westly]] – [[California State Controller]]; former Internet executive The two front-runners for the Democratic nomination were Angelides and [[California State Controller]] [[Steve Westly]]. A pre-election poll had Westly leading Angelides by six percentage points.{{Cite web|date=April 2006|title=Special Survey on Education|url=https://www.ppic.org/content/pubs/survey/S_406MBS.pdf|url-status=live|website=ppic.org|publisher=Public Policy Institute of California|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060507222622/http://www.ppic.org/content/pubs/survey/S_406MBS.pdf |archive-date=2006-05-07 }} The Field Poll conducted on April 17, 2006, showed that both Democratic candidates had low recognition factors amongst the state's electorate, with only 45% having any opinion on Angelides and 40% for Westly. Of registered Democrats surveyed, 59% said they didn't know enough about Angelides to have any opinion about him, with 58% saying the same for Westly.{{cite web |url=http://field.com/fieldpollonline/subscribers/RLS2193.pdf |title=RLS2193 for PDF.PDF |access-date=2010-08-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101020150806/http://field.com/fieldpollonline/subscribers/RLS2193.pdf |archive-date=2010-10-20 |url-status=dead }} The ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' reported that the race for the Democratic nomination was a virtual tie, with Angelides leading Westly by three percentage points (37%–34%), within the 3% margin of error. Unusually, 28% of Democratic voters were undecided, and both candidates tried to earn the undecided vote. Angelides reported a recent increase in support for his campaign and gained union support as well as support from the "core" [[Liberalism in the United States|liberal]] constituency. The [[California Democratic Party]] endorsed him prior to the primary, despite most polls showing that Westly would fare much better against Schwarzenegger in the general election.{{Cite web|url=https://investortimes.com/progressreport/9269-2/|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070509222636/http://www.californiaprogressreport.com/2006/04/angelides_endor.html|url-status=dead|title=Penny Wise Pound Foolish – Cuts in Free Flu Vaccines|first=Progress|last=Report|date=August 17, 2011|archivedate=May 9, 2007}} However, many registered Democrats believed that Westly had a greater chance of winning against incumbent governor Schwarzenegger and felt that he had a slightly "more positive" image.{{cite web |url=https://www.latimes.com/la-me-poll28may28,0,5948271.story?coll=la-story-footer |archive-url=https://wayback.archive-it.org/all/20170525040730/http://articles.latimes.com/2006/may/28/local/me-poll28 |url-status=dead |archive-date=2017-05-25 |title=Angelides Pulls Even With Westly – Los Angeles Times |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=2006-05-28 |access-date=2010-08-14 }} In the end, Angelides won 47.9% of the vote to Westly's 43.4%. Noonan]] ([[American Independent Party|American Independent]]) – computer shop owner * [[Art Olivier]] ([[Libertarian Party of California|Libertarian]]) – former mayor of [[Bellflower, California|Bellflower]], 2000 Libertarian Party vice presidential candidate ([[Harry Browne]]'s running mate) * [[Arnold Schwarzenegger]] ([[California Republican Party|Republican]]) – incumbent [[Governor of California]], actor, businessman === Campaign === Schwarzenegger's decision to call the [[California special election, 2005|2005 special election]], as well as his propositions dealing with teachers' and [[nurse]]s' [[trade union|unions]] and other political missteps, brought his approval rating down to 39% by April 2006,{{Cite web|date=13 April 2006|title=Schwarzenegger approval rating: 39 percent|url=http://www.ocregister.com/ocregister/news/state/stateelections/article_1100965.php|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930182418/http://www.ocregister.com/ocregister/news/state/stateelections/article_1100965.php|archive-date=2007-09-30|access-date=2006-04-25|website=ocregister.com}} though he ended up solidly defeating his opponents. During his first two years, he came under fire from some conservatives for supporting several taxes on Californians,{{Cite news|last1=Halper|first1=Evan|last2=Rau|first2=Jordan|date=7 November 2008|title=Gov. pushes hike in sales tax, big cuts|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2008-nov-07-me-arnold7-story.html|access-date=18 September 2020}} and from some [[American liberalism|liberals]] for refusing to sign a bill allowing [[Same-sex marriage in the United States|gay marriage]], and his support for several controversial propositions in 2005. {{collapse bottom}} ==Analysis== Results showed Schwarzenegger won 52 counties while Angelides won six; Schwarzenegger won an absolute majority in 48 counties and a plurality in four others, while Angelides won a majority in two counties and a plurality in four more. Schwarzenegger won large majorities in California's rural counties, the populous [[Southern California]] counties of [[San Diego County, California|San Diego]], [[Orange County, California|Orange]], [[Riverside County, California|Riverside]], [[San Bernardino County, California|San Bernardino]], and [[Ventura County, California|Ventura]], as well as populous [[Sacramento County, California|Sacramento]], [[Fresno County, California|Fresno]], and [[Kern County, California|Kern]] counties in the [[Central Valley (California)|Central Valley]]. The results were closely contested in [[Los Angeles County, California|Los Angeles County]] and in [[San Francisco Bay Area|Bay Area]] suburban counties. Angelides won substantially only in [[Alameda County, California|Alameda]] and [[San Francisco]] counties.
